lines.text: Which of these displaces the oxygen–haemoglobin dissociation curve to the left?
The answer is a fall in p C O two.
A left shift means haemoglobin grips its oxygen tightly, like this strong hero hugging every ball.
The carbon dioxide balloon deflates. A fall in p C O two shifts the curve left.
(laugh) His friend waves the flag for a rise in p H, another left shift.
So do a fall in temperature, less two three D P G, fetal haemoglobin, and carbon monoxide.
Acidosis, heat, a rise in p C O two, and exercise push it right.
Remember: a fall in p C O two shifts the curve to the left.
